candidates.description: Restate the subquestion as an explicit input-output-decision problem.
candidates.acceptance: The paper states what is predicted, optimized, ranked, classified, or explained.

candidates.description: Connect model output to a loss, utility, feasibility, or ranking criterion.
candidates.acceptance: The objective or decision rule is written as a formula and checked numerically.

candidates.description: Carry sampling, parameter, scenario, or measurement uncertainty into the final result.
candidates.acceptance: The final result has an interval, sensitivity table, or scenario comparison.

candidates.description: Design figures around claims rather than around available plotting routines.
candidates.acceptance: Every formal figure is referenced by a claim in the evidence map.
